mainTopic: שחוטי חוץ: when an animal counts as fit inside — הואיל, עקירה, and a פסח slaughtered outside during the year
overview: This amud deals with שחוטי חוץ: one is liable for slaughtering an animal outside the מקדש only if it was fit to be offered inside at that moment. רב חסדא finishes his ruling on the יום כפור goats: before the היכל doors are opened, slaughtering them outside is פטור, because מחוסר פתיחה is like מחוסר מעשה. The גמרא asks whether רב חסדא holds of הואיל, since his ruling on a פסח slaughtered outside during the year implies that a סתמא פסח is פטור. It answers that a פסח needs עקירה to become a שלמים, while the goats need none. Then two reports of רבי יוחנן arrive. רב דימי says a פסח slaughtered outside during the year is פטור either way, because עקירת חוץ is not an עקירה. רבין says it is חייב either way, because a פסח during the year is already a שלמים. רב אשי and רב ירמיה מדפתי disagree over the שלא לשמו case, which shows a dispute with רב חלקיה בר טובי about whether an עקירה done outside counts. Finally the גמרא returns to the goats after the lottery and begins a ברייתא on the verse of שחוטי חוץ, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Slaughtered outside before the היכל doors opened: exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא continues: if the יום כפור goats were slaughtered outside before the היכל doors were opened, he is פטור. The reason is that מחוסר פתיחה counts like מחוסר מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered them outside before the doors of the Sanctuary were opened, he is exempt. Why? Lacking the opening of the doors is like lacking an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב חסדא's ruling about the יום כפור goats. It adds a case where slaughtering them outside brings no liability, and it gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You are only liable for שחוטי חוץ if the animal could have been offered inside right now. A קרבן cannot be slaughtered inside while the היכל doors are closed. So at that moment the animal is not fit inside. Since something still has to be done before it becomes fit, it is like an animal that still needs an action, and it does not count as fit.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered them outside the מקדש (שחוטי חוץ)
The doors of the Sanctuary building
Exempt (no liability)
Lacking the opening (of the doors)
Lacking an action: something still has to be done before the item is fit

steps.confusionAlert: Being פטור here does not mean the animal stopped being a קרבן. It is still a קרבן. The point is only that at that moment it was not yet fit to be offered inside, so the special liability of שחוטי חוץ does not apply.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered them outside before were opened
phrases.notes: "Them" means the שעירי יום הכפורים from רב חסדא's earlier statement.

phrases.english: the doors of the Sanctuary, he is exempt.
What is the reason?
Lacking the opening is considered like lacking an action.
phrases.notes: So the animal was not yet fit inside, and there is no liability outside

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָן בַּחוּץ קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּפְתְּחוּ דַּלְתוֹת הַהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חסדא's statement on the previous amud, where he made the goats liable before the הגרלה because of הואיל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering the יום כפור goats outside before the היכל doors open is פטור, because מחוסר פתיחה is treated as מחוסר מעשה.

steps.title: Does רב חסדא really hold of the principle of 'since'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב חסדא accepts the reasoning of הואיל, which he used for the goats before the lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רב חסדא really hold of "since"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a doubt about the reasoning רב חסדא used earlier. This line is a setup: the next step brings a source to show the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the lottery, רב חסדא said one is liable because הואיל: the goats could still be used as the מוסף goat, so we treat them as fit. The גמרא now questions whether רב חסדא really holds of this kind of reasoning anywhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: "And does he hold of…?" A question that usually leads into a challenge
"Since": since it could be fit in another way, we treat it as fit now

phrases.english: And does Rav Chisda hold of
"since"?
phrases.notes: Refers to his reason for liability before the הגרלה

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַב חִסְדָּא הוֹאִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning (הואיל) that sits behind רב חסדא's ruling about the goats.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is הואיל a principle that רב חסדא consistently accepts?

steps.title: רב חסדא's ruling on a Pesach slaughtered outside during the year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another ruling of רב חסדא. A פסח slaughtered outside during the year לשמו is פטור, but שלא לשמו is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חסדא say: A פסח that someone slaughtered outside during the rest of the year: if for its own sake, he is exempt. If not for its own sake, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different statement of רב חסדא. It will be used as the source for the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the year, a פסח cannot be offered as a פסח, so slaughtering it outside as a פסח is not slaughtering a fit קרבן, and he is פטור. But if it is slaughtered as a שלמים (שלא לשמו), it would be valid inside. So slaughtering it outside that way makes him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: "But didn't he say…?" Introduces a source to challenge with
The Paschal lamb (קרבן פסח)
During the rest of the year (not ערב פסח)
For its own sake (as the offering it was meant to be)
Not for its own sake (here: as a שלמים)

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chisda say:
A Paschal lamb that he slaughtered outside
during the rest of the days of the year,
for its own sake, he is exempt,
phrases.notes: It is not fit as a פסח at this time of year

phrases.english: not for its own sake, he is liable.
phrases.notes: As a שלמים it would be valid inside

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source text that will show רב חסדא does not seem to use הואיל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered outside during the year is פטור if slaughtered לשמו and חייב if slaughtered שלא לשמו.

steps.title: Unspecified slaughter is exempt, so why not apply 'since'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רב חסדא's words that slaughtering the פסח with no stated intent (סתמא) counts as לשמו and is פטור. It then challenges: we should say הואיל, since it is fit inside as שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he is liable is only because it was not for its own sake. But if it was unspecified, it counts as for its own sake, and he is exempt. Why? Let us say: since it is fit inside when slaughtered not for its own sake, he should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into רב חסדא's ruling about the פסח. It finds a case where he does not apply הואיל, which clashes with his ruling about the יום כפור goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רב חסדא made liability depend on saying שלא לשמו, it follows that slaughtering it with no stated intent is פטור. But if רב חסדא held of הואיל, he should say: since this animal could be validly offered inside as a שלמים, it counts as fit, and he should be חייב even without saying so. This seems to show that רב חסדא does not hold of הואיל, which contradicts his ruling about the goats.

keyTerms.meaning: "The reason is because…": a close reading that implies the opposite case
"But if unspecified": no stated intent
"But why?" Begins the attack
"Let us say"
Inside the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא used הואיל to make the goats חייב before the הגרלה. But his פסח ruling implies he does not use הואיל for a פסח slaughtered סתמא. The גמרא now needs to resolve this contradiction.
steps.confusionAlert: The challenge does not come from what רב חסדא said outright. It comes from what his words imply: a פסח slaughtered סתמא, with no stated intent, counts as לשמו and is therefore פטור.

phrases.english: The reason is that it was not for its own sake,
but if unspecified, it is for its own sake and he is exempt.
phrases.notes: A פסח slaughtered with no stated intent counts as a פסח

phrases.english: But why?
Let us say: since
it is fit inside when slaughtered not for its own sake!
phrases.notes: As a שלמים, so he should be liable

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ הָא סְתָמָא לִשְׁמוֹ הוּא וּפָטוּר וְאַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads closely into the quoted ruling and turns it into a contradiction with רב חסדא's use of הואיל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's use of הואיל to make the יום כפור goats חייב before the הגרלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His פסח ruling implies that slaughtering סתמא is פטור. That means he does not say הואיל there, even though the animal is fit inside as a שלמים. So his two rulings seem inconsistent.

steps.title: The פסח Needs Re-Designation, the Goats Do Not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. A פסח cannot become a שלמים without עקירה, but the יום כפור goats can be offered as חטאות without any change.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! There (the פסח) needs to be uprooted from its identity. This one (the goats) does not need to be uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 4 by showing that the פסח case and the goat case are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח slaughtered with no stated intent is still a פסח, and a פסח during the year is not fit. It only becomes fit as a שלמים if someone actively uproots it with שלא לשמו intent. The יום כפור goats are already חטאות, just like the מוסף goats, so they can be offered as מוסף goats as they are, with no re-designation. So the goats count as fit right now, and the ruling about them does not really depend on a broad הואיל that could also reach a סתמא פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: How can these be compared?! (rejects a comparison)
Uprooting: actively removing an offering from its original designation
There (the other case)

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not prove that רב חסדא holds a general principle of הואיל. It shows that the goats need no עקירה: they are already fit as חטאות, like the מוסף goats. A סתמא פסח, by contrast, would need an עקירה before it could be fit as a שלמים, so there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
There (the Passover offering) requires uprooting,
phrases.notes: Without שלא לשמו intent, it stays a פסח and is unfit.

phrases.english: this (the goats) does not require uprooting.
phrases.notes: They are already sin-offerings, just like the additional-offering goats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If הואיל works for the goats, it should also make a סתמא פסח count as fit, since it could be a שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The goats are fit as מוסף חטאות without any עקירה, so they count as fit. A סתמא פסח needs עקירה to become a שלמים, so it is not fit, and the two rulings do not contradict each other.

steps.title: The Same Rulings Taught in the Name of רבה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שימי taught these rulings in the name of רבה instead of רב חסדא. He noticed the same contradiction and resolved it the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שימי taught them in the name of רבה. He found a contradiction between one ruling of רבה and another ruling of רבה, and he resolved it as we resolved it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a note that there is another version of who said these rulings. It is the same discussion with a different name attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole exchange (goats, פסח, הואיל, עקירה) stays the same. Only the author changes from רב חסדא to רבה. The question and the answer repeat exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught them (the rulings)
He found a contradiction between two statements of רבה
And he answered as we answered

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר שִׁימִי מַתְנֵי לְהוּ בִּדְרַבָּה,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Shimi taught them in the name of Rabba,
and he found a contradiction between Rabba and Rabba.
And he resolved it as we resolved it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר שִׁימִי מַתְנֵי לְהוּ בִּדְרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate attribution for the discussion that step 5 just closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rulings and the answer belong to רבה in this version. The content does not change.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Slaughtering a פסח Outside During the Year Is Exempt Either Way
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי brings a teaching from ארץ ישראל in the name of רבי יוחנן. A פסח slaughtered outside during the year is פטור, whether it was לשמו or שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי ירמיה, in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone slaughtered a פסח outside during the rest of the year, whether for its own sake or not for its own sake, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching that disagrees with רב חסדא's ruling from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that שלא לשמו makes the person חייב, because the animal becomes a fit שלמים. רבי יוחנן says the person is פטור even when it was שלא לשמו. This sets up the next question: why is it not fit as a שלמים?

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
During the rest of the days of the year (not ערב פסח)
Whether for its own sake or not for its own sake

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a direct disagreement with רב חסדא about שלא לשמו. The rest of the sugya now has to explain רבי יוחנן's position.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A Passover offering that one slaughtered outside
during the rest of the days of the year,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִשְׁמוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ — פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: whether for its own sake or not for its own sake, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new opinion that contrasts with רב חסדא's ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered outside during the year is פטור, whether לשמו or שלא לשמו.

steps.title: רב דימי Questions the Exemption for Not-For-Its-Own-Sake
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי accepts that לשמו is פטור, because a פסח is not fit during the year. He asks why שלא לשמו should be פטור, since it is fit inside as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי said: I said this teaching before רבי ירמיה and asked: It makes sense for לשמו, because it is not fit. But for שלא לשמו, why is he exempt? It is fit שלא לשמו inside!
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי challenges the second half of רבי יוחנן's ruling. The next step gives רבי ירמיה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You are only חייב for slaughtering outside if the animal was fit to be offered inside. A פסח לשמו is not fit during the year, so פטור makes sense. A פסח שלא לשמו is offered inside as a valid שלמים, so it seems fit, and the person should be חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: I said the teaching (presented it)
It makes sense regarding... (sets up a contrast)
Not fit
Inside (in the עזרה, the Temple courtyard)

phrases.english: Rav Dimi said:
I said this teaching before Rabbi Yirmeya
Granted, for its own sake,
because it is not fit (as a Passover offering now).
But not for its own sake, why (is he exempt)?
Isn't it fit not for its own sake inside?
phrases.notes: Inside, it would be a valid peace-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לִשְׁמוֹ, דְּהָא לָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ. אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ, אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the שלא לשמו half of רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a פסח slaughtered outside שלא לשמו during the year is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability for slaughtering outside depends on the animal being fit inside. A פסח שלא לשמו is fit inside as a שלמים, so the person should be חייב.

steps.title: Changing an offering's identity outside does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers רב דימי: an עקירה done outside the מקדש is not considered an עקירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: uprooting outside is not called uprooting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי reports the answer he received to his question from Step 8. Uprooting the פסח's identity outside the מקדש does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי had asked why a פסח slaughtered outside שלא לשמו is פטור, since it could serve as a שלמים inside. The answer is that the שלא לשמו intent outside does not turn it into a שלמים. It stays a פסח, which is not fit during the year, so it is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Uprooting, meaning removing an offering from its original identity, for example through שלא לשמו intent
An uprooting that happens outside the מקדש
It is not called, so it does not count as

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי יוחנן (in רב דימי's version) made both cases פטור. Outside the מקדש, intent cannot convert a פסח into a שלמים.

phrases.english: And he said to me:
phrases.notes: רבי ירמיה answering רב דימי

phrases.english: Uprooting outside is not called uprooting.
phrases.notes: So the פסח does not become a שלמים

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב דימי's question from Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle limiting the power of עקירה to inside the מקדש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלא לשמו turns the פסח into a שלמים, which is fit inside, so one should be חייב
steps.terutzMaskana: Outside, עקירה does not work. The animal stays a פסח, which is unfit during the year, so one is פטור.

steps.title: רבין's version: liable in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that slaughtering a פסח outside during the year makes one חייב, whether לשמו or שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי ירמיה, in the name of רבי יוחנן: a פסח slaughtered outside during the rest of the year makes one liable, whether it was for its own sake or not.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of רבי יוחנן's teaching arrives from ארץ ישראל, this time through רבין. It gives the opposite result from רב דימי's version: חייב in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's version said פטור in both cases. רבין's version says חייב in both cases. The surprising part is לשמו, because a פסח is not fit as a פסח during the year.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Liable, here for the sin of שחוטי חוץ
The rest of the days of the year, meaning not on ערב פסח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reporters. רב דימי's version says פטור in both cases, and רבין's version says חייב in both cases. Both quote רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: When Ravin came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: he said: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A Pesach offering that one slaughtered outside
during the rest of the days of the year,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִשְׁמוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: whether for its own sake or not for its own sake, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the teaching רב דימי reported in Step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered outside during the year makes one חייב, whether לשמו or שלא לשמו

steps.title: Challenge: an offering that is not yet in its time is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the לשמו part of רבין's version from a משנה that exempts offerings lacking time, whether the lack is in the animal or in the owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even for its own sake? But we learned in a משנה: an offering lacking time, whether in its own body or because of its owners, is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that one would be חייב even for לשמו. It starts quoting a משנה about offerings that are 'lacking time' to show that such offerings are פטור when slaughtered outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone is only חייב for slaughtering outside if the offering could have been brought inside right now. The גמרא quotes this משנה about offerings that are not yet in their time because, together with רב חלקיה בר טובי's comment on it (step 14), it shows a case where an animal fit inside שלא לשמו is still פטור when slaughtered לשמו. That will be the real attack on רבין in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking time, meaning an offering not yet ready to be brought
In its own body, for example an animal less than eight days old
Through the owners, when the owner is not yet allowed to bring it

phrases.english: And even for its own sake?
phrases.notes: This is asked in surprise.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: lacking time —
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה in מסכת זבחים

phrases.english: whether in its body or in its owners.
phrases.notes: The משנה's ruling, that he is exempt (פטור), comes in the next line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the לשמו ruling of רבין's version from Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's claim that a פסח slaughtered outside לשמו during the year makes one חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה, as read by רב חלקיה בר טובי, makes an אשם slaughtered outside לשמו פטור even though it would be fit inside שלא לשמו. So being fit in another way should not make a פסח slaughtered לשמו חייב either.

steps.title: The משנה defines owners who are lacking time
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה explains which cases count as 'lacking time through the owners': a זב, a זבה, a יולדת, and a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is an offering lacking time through its owners? A זב, a זבה, a woman after childbirth, and a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The quote from the משנה continues and defines its own term. This sets up the comparison the גמרא needs: here the animal is fine, but the timing is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people must wait a fixed period before bringing their offerings. If they bring them too early, the offering is 'lacking time' even though nothing is wrong with the animal. This is closest to a פסח during the year: the animal is fine, but it is the wrong time for a פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a certain bodily discharge who must count seven clean days before bringing his offering
The female equivalent of a זב
A woman after childbirth, who brings her offering when her purification period ends
A person with צרעת, who brings offerings after counting seven days

phrases.english: And what is lacking time through the owners —
the zav and the zavah
and the woman after childbirth and the metzora
phrases.notes: The quote continues into the next passage

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה quoted in Step 11 by defining 'lacking time through the owners'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offering is 'lacking time through the owners' when people like a זב, זבה, יולדת, or מצורע bring it before their required waiting period is over

steps.title: The משנה's ruling: חטאת and אשם exempt, עולה and שלמים liable
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה rules that if these not-yet-ready owners bring their חטאת and אשם outside, they are פטור. If they bring their עולה and שלמים outside, they are חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those who offered their sin-offering and guilt-offering outside are exempt. If they offered their burnt-offerings and peace-offerings outside, they are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה it is using to challenge רבין. It gives the ruling for the זב, זבה, יולדת, and מצורע who sacrificed outside before their time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת and an אשם cannot be brought as voluntary gifts, so before the owner's time they are not fit inside at all. Bringing them outside is therefore פטור. An עולה or שלמים could be accepted inside as a voluntary gift, so bringing them outside is חייב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 12 by giving its ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Owners lacking time are פטור for a חטאת or אשם brought outside, and חייב for an עולה or שלמים brought outside.

steps.title: רב חלקיה בר טובי limits the exemption to לשמו
steps.stepSummary: רב חלקיה בר טובי says the פטור for the אשם applies only when it was slaughtered לשמו. If it was slaughtered שלא לשמו, the person is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חלקיה בר טובי said: They only taught this when it was done for its own sake. But if it was done not for its own sake, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a limit to the משנה's ruling about the אשם. The פטור applies only when it was slaughtered as an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם slaughtered inside שלא לשמו is still a valid offering. So when slaughtered outside שלא לשמו, it counts as something fit inside, and one is חייב. Notice that this treats a change of purpose made outside as effective.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught [this ruling] in the case of
For its own sake, as the offering it was designated for
Not for its own sake, as a different offering
Liable

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement becomes the base of both the coming challenge (step 15) and the final note that רב ירמיה מדפתי argues with it (step 19).

phrases.english: And Rav Chilkiya bar Tovi said:
They only taught this when it was for its own sake,
but if it was not for its own sake, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's פטור for the אשם to the case of לשמו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם of an owner lacking time, slaughtered outside שלא לשמו, makes one חייב.

steps.title: Why not make the guilt-offering לשמו liable too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: at least לשמו is פטור, but why? We should say that since it would be fit inside שלא לשמו, he is חייב even לשמו. That is exactly how רבין made a פסח לשמו חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, for its own sake he is exempt. Why? Let us say: since they are fit inside not for their own sake, he should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual challenge against רבין's version. If 'fit in another way' makes one חייב, then the אשם לשמו should be חייב too, yet the משנה says it is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין said a פסח slaughtered outside לשמו during the year is חייב, because it could be valid as a שלמים. By the same logic, an אשם לשמו should be חייב, because it could be valid inside שלא לשמו. Since even רב חלקיה agrees the אשם לשמו is פטור, רבין's logic seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: At least, in any case
Why?
Since
Fit
Inside the מקדש

phrases.english: For its own sake, at least, he is exempt. Why?
Let us say: since they are fit
not for their own sake inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the agreed פטור of the אשם לשמו to attack רבין's logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's report (step 10) that a פסח slaughtered outside לשמו during the year makes one חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being fit inside in another way creates liability, the אשם לשמו should be חייב. The משנה says it is פטור, so 'fit in another way' should not create liability for the פסח either.

steps.title: An אשם needs עקירה; a פסח during the year is automatically a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. An אשם becomes valid only through an active עקירה. A פסח during the year is already a שלמים by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that comparable?! There, it needs uprooting. Here, a פסח during the rest of the year is a peace-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבין by showing the two cases are different. The comparison in step 15 does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם slaughtered לשמו was never uprooted from being an אשם, so it was not fit inside as it was done. A פסח during the year automatically has the status of a שלמים, even if it was slaughtered לשמו. So it truly is fit, and רבין's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that comparable?! (rejects a comparison)
Uprooting: actively changing an offering away from its original designation
There / here
The rest of the days of the year (not ערב פסח)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the פסח stops being in the category of a פסח. The point is only how it is treated during the year: it is handled like a שלמים without needing any active change.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, it needs uprooting;
here, a Pesach during the rest of the days of the year
is a peace-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by distinguishing the אשם from the פסח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the אשם and the פסח are 'fit inside in another way,' so they should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אשם needs active עקירה, which did not happen when it was slaughtered לשמו. A פסח during the year is automatically a שלמים, so it is fit even לשמו.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבין, a פסח during the year is a שלמים automatically, with no עקירה needed. That is why slaughtering it outside, even לשמו, makes one חייב.

steps.title: רב אשי: a פסח slaughtered outside שלא לשמו is liable
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי teaches that one who slaughters a פסח outside during the year שלא לשמו is חייב, just as we explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי taught: He is liable, as we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings two versions of the ruling for a פסח slaughtered outside during the year שלא לשמו. רב אשי's version says חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'As we said' points to the earlier reasoning: a פסח during the year is a שלמים, and it is surely fit when slaughtered שלא לשמו. So slaughtering it outside makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught, transmitted the version
As we said earlier

phrases.english: Rav Ashi taught:
He is liable, as we said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a dispute of versions about the שלא לשמו case of a פסח during the year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered outside during the year שלא לשמו makes one חייב.

steps.title: רב ירמיה מדפתי: exempt, because uprooting outside is not uprooting
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדפתי teaches פטור. He holds that a פסח during the year still needs עקירה, and an עקירה done outside the מקדש does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה of Difti taught: He is exempt. He holds that a פסח during the rest of the year needs uprooting, and uprooting outside is not called uprooting.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the opposing version. רב ירמיה מדפתי says the person is פטור and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning has two parts. First, a פסח during the year is not automatically a שלמים; it needs an active עקירה. Second, an עקירה done outside is not effective, so the animal never became fit, and there is no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: From דפתי (a town in בבל)
He holds, his reasoning is
Uprooting done outside the מקדש
Is not called, does not count as

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya of Difti taught: He is exempt.
He holds: a Pesach during the rest of the days of the year
needs uprooting,
and uprooting outside is not called uprooting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite version from רב אשי's, with reasoning matching רבי ירמיה's answer in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered outside during the year שלא לשמו is פטור, since it needs עקירה and an עקירה outside does not work.

steps.title: This view argues with רב חלקיה בר טובי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב ירמיה מדפתי's view disagrees with רב חלקיה בר טובי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב חלקיה בר טובי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes by pointing out a conflict. רב ירמיה מדפתי's reasoning cannot fit with רב חלקיה's ruling about the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חלקיה made an אשם slaughtered outside שלא לשמו חייב, even though an אשם needs עקירה. That means he holds an עקירה done outside does count. רב ירמיה מדפתי says it does not count, so the two disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees with

steps.whatToRemember: The core dispute is whether an עקירה done outside the מקדש counts. רב חלקיה בר טובי holds it does, so שלא לשמו is חייב. רב ירמיה מדפתי holds it does not, so שלא לשמו is פטור.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Chilkiya bar Tovi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the consequence of רב ירמיה מדפתי's reasoning against step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ירמיה מדפתי, who holds that an עקירה outside is not an עקירה, argues with רב חלקיה בר טובי, who treats an עקירה outside as effective.

steps.title: Returning to the ruling on the two goats after the lottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the earlier ברייתא: once the lots are drawn, one who slaughters outside is חייב for the goat of ה' and פטור for the goat of עזאזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: After he drew the lots on them, he is חייב for the goat that is for ה', and פטור for the goat that is for עזאזל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the earlier ברייתא so it can now examine it. This is a setup line that prepares the next move: finding the source for this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the lottery, one is liable for either goat, because (as רב חסדא explained) each could still be used as the מוסף goat. After the lottery, only the goat of ה' is going to be offered on the מזבח. The goat of עזאזל is sent away to the wilderness, not offered as a קרבן to ה', so slaughtering it outside is not the sin of שחוטי חוץ.

keyTerms.meaning: He drew the lots that decide which goat is for ה' and which is for עזאזל
The goat designated "for the Name", meaning for ה'. It is offered as a קרבן
The goat designated for עזאזל. It is sent off to the wilderness and is not offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: פטור for the goat of עזאזל does not mean it is allowed to slaughter it. It only means there is no punishment of שחוטי חוץ, because that goat is not offered as a קרבן on the מזבח.

steps.title: A ברייתא quotes the verse of slaughtering outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that quotes ויקרא 17:3–4, the source for the sin of שחוטי חוץ. This sets up an exact reading of the verse's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "Any man of the house of ישראל who slaughters an ox, a sheep, or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters outside the camp, and did not bring it to the entrance of the אהל מועד to offer it as a קרבן to ה'..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a ברייתא by quoting the Torah's verse about slaughtering a קרבן outside the מקדש. This is setup. The ברייתא will now explain each phrase of the verse, and that will give the source for the rule about the two goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse makes one liable only for an animal that should have been brought "to the entrance of the אהל מועד" as a קרבן "to ה'". Words like these can leave out the goat for עזאזל, which is never brought there as a קרבן. The exact reading of the verse continues on the next amud.

"To ה'": a phrase that limits the law to something offered to ה'

steps.whyThisMatters: This verse is the main source for the whole law of שחוטי חוץ. Each of its phrases will be read closely to decide which animals make a person liable.
